index.headline: One offer,
index.intro: Build ships and sharpens the site. Growth compounds the traffic and the AI answers. Most teams start on one track — the strongest run both, because the site you ship feeds the traffic you grow, and back again.

index.bothText: Run one track or both. When you run both, the same team owns the whole loop — nothing gets re-briefed between the people who build and the people who grow.

clarifier.intro: “SEO/AEO” and “GEO” get used interchangeably. They answer two different questions — and need two different programs.

seo.question: Is your site found?
seo.bodySuffix: rank on Google and get pulled into AI Overviews, ChatGPT, and Perplexity when someone searches your category. The work lives on your site; the win is your page showing up.

geo.question: Does AI recommend you?
geo.bodyPrefix: When a buyer asks an AI “which vendor should we use?”, GEO is the work that makes
geo.bodySuffix: the name it returns — whether or not your page ranks. It’s about being the answer, not owning the link.
geo.unitSuffix: — how often AI names you, across engines.
geo.proof: How we took Toku from unranked to cited by name — that’s the exhibit above.

items.question: Can I hire you for just one service?
items.answer: Yes. An engagement can start with GEO, SEO, AEO, content, conversion, or stack-specific delivery. We add work when it supports the result. The same team keeps the context as the scope grows.

items.question: What’s the real difference between SEO/AEO and GEO?
items.answer: SEO/AEO makes your own pages visible in search and AI answers — measured in rankings and citations of your URLs. GEO makes AI engines recommend you by name when buyers ask who to hire — measured as share of answer. Related work, different scoreboards. The panel above lays it out side by side.

items.question: Do the build team and the growth team actually talk?
items.answer: They’re the same team. The people who ship your site are the people who run its SEO, conversion, and AI-visibility work — so the site is built to be found and to convert from day one, not retrofitted later.

items.question: How fast do you respond?
items.answer: Within about two hours during working hours. You get one team and a direct line, not a ticket queue that routes your question to whoever’s free.

items.question: How do we start?
items.answer: A 30-minute strategy call. We look at your site together and tell you which of the nine services it actually needs, which to skip, and where they would move the needle first. No pitch deck.
